title: TSMC Plans Up to 20% Price Hike for CoWoS Advanced Packaging
summary:
Lead times for semiconductor packaging equipment have increased to 8 months as foundries struggle to keep pace with the demand for AI hardware. The supply crunch has led TSMC to prepare a price increase of up to 20% for its Chip on Wafer on Substrate (CoWoS) advanced packaging, reports citing supply chain sources say.

The cost adjustment comes as the use of CoWoS, which connects AI processors to high-bandwidth memory, expands beyond GPUs to include server CPUs and custom ASICs. TSMC Chairman C.C. Wei stated that packages five times the size of the largest printable chip are already in mass production. Monthly CoWoS capacity is estimated to exceed 130,000 wafers this year and reach 200,000 wafers by 2027.

selectedTweets.text:
TSMC is reportedly preparing another CoWoS price rise of up to 20% as AI packaging demand outruns supply.

CoWoS (Chip on Wafer on Substrate), joins an AI processor to its high-bandwidth memory on one densely wired base.

Demand has spread from GPUs to server CPUs and custom ASICs, so foundries and packagers expect 10% to 20% increases.

Supply can’t jump quickly, since equipment lead times stretched from 3-6 months to 6-8 months, and tool buyers no longer haggle.

Larger packages will deepen the squeeze, because they cut each tool’s hourly output, so even flat chip volumes need more machines.

They keep growing: TSMC chairman C.C. Wei says packages 5 times the largest printable chip are in mass production at excellent yields, with 9x and 14x planned.
